newsitem.title: FRANCE: France okays high-speed Paris-Strasbourg rail link.
newsitem.headline: France okays high-speed Paris-Strasbourg rail link.

text.p: France said on Thursday it will go ahead with construction of a high-speed rail between Paris and the northeastern city of Strasbourg despite its high price-tag.
But the line will be built gradually, over an as-yet unspecified calendar, to stretch out costs, Transport Minister Bernard Pons said.
Pons told the Senate Finance Committee that the government would go ahead with the "TGV-East", enabling travel between the French capital and the home of the European parliament in two hours' time.
He said a slower but cheaper alternative tehcnology, relying on existing rail lines and a so-called tilting train, had been rejected.
"The government's goal is to build a new rail line from Paris to Strasbourg on a phased-in basis," Pons said.
France's celebrated high-speed trains streak across the countryside at cruising speeds of 300 km (190 miles) an hour.
But the high cost of building the special rail lines has strained the budget at a time of spending austerity intended to help France qualify for a single European currency.

Philippe Rouvillois, former chairman of the SNCF state railway authority, recently recommended that France switch to the so-called tilting train or Pendolino pioneered by Italy's Fiat Ferroviaria, which runs on normal rail lines but at a slower speed than TGVs.

New SNCF chairman Louis Gallois recently acknowledged that experts had concluded the planned TGV-East line would be less profitable than previously forecast but said it was up to the government to decide whether to go ahead with its construction.
